title: One STAR story in two to three minutes: where the time goes
captions: Start with just enough context: the team, the system and why the problem mattered. About 20 seconds. Weak stories often spend far too long here.
Say what your goal was and what your part was. About 15 seconds. The listener now knows what to judge you on.
Spend most of the time on your actions. Say what you did, which options you saw, and why you chose one. Use “I” for your own work.
End with the result. Give a number if you have one, then one thing you learned. Without this part, the interviewer has no outcome to write down.
Stop and let the interviewer ask. Follow-up questions are where they check the details. A true story holds up here; a vague one does not.
